name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the central nervous system
aliases: Primary CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in immunocompromised patients, including HIV-positive individuals

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) criteria for PCNSL

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in CNS tissue biopsy
MRI showing solitary or multiple enhancing lesions within the brain parenchyma without systemic lymphoma evidence
Exclusion of systemic lymphoma by whole-body imaging and bone marrow biopsy
Cerebrospinal fluid cytology and flow cytometry supporting lymphoma diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus typical MRI findings and exclusion of systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary approach including neuro-oncology, radiology, and pathology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cognitive impairment including memory loss and confusion

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances including diplopia or blurred vision
Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
opportunistic infections due to low immunity
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Spinal cord involvement causing limb weakness
searchTerms: limb weakness due to spinal involvement

laboratory: CSF cytology positive for malignant lymphoid cells
CSF flow cytometry showing clonal B-cell population
imaging: MRI brain with contrast showing homogeneously enhancing lesions, often periventricular
Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) showing restricted diffusion in lesions
genetic: MYC and BCL2 gene alterations in some cases
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD79a, and MUM1
High Ki-67 proliferation index in tumor cells

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology shows glial origin cells rather than lymphoid
MRI often shows ring-enhancing lesions with central necrosis
Presence of known primary malignancy outside CNS
Multiple lesions with variable enhancement patterns
Systemic imaging positive for extracranial tumors
MRI lesions typically periventricular and ovoid, not mass-like
CSF oligoclonal bands present without malignant cells
Clinical course relapsing-remitting rather than progressive mass effect

redFlags: New onset seizures in elderly or immunocompromised patients
Focal neurological deficits with mass effect on imaging
references: Ferreri AJM. Primary CNS lymphoma. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2017;2017(1):401-408.
Batchelor TT, Loeffler JS. Primary CNS lymphoma. J Clin Oncol. 2006;24(8):1281-1288.
Grommes C, DeAngelis LM. Primary CNS lymphoma. J Clin Oncol. 2017;35(21):2410-2418.
